title: Gate Cadence Stitchboard: Roadmap checkpoints, KPIs, and contingency notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight operational "stitchboard" for coordinating product-ops, infra, SRE and customer success across release gates. It's intended to be used alongside the formal launch playbook; think of it as the cadence calendar + decision checklist + fast-contingency notes that we update during runway.

When to use:
- Early planning (T-90 to T-30): align owners, target KPIs, and test plans.
- Preflight (T-14 to T-3): confirm telemetry, smoke tests, and rollback criteria.
- Launch window (T-2 to T+7): use as operational checklist and source of truth for gate decisions.

Key principles (working assumptions):
- Keep gates narrow and binary (go / no-go / hold) with clear metric thresholds.
- Prefer fast mitigations that remove risk while preserving availability (route to fallback model variant, limit traffic, reduce sequence length).
- Trace ownership: every gate line must list the accountable owner and at least one deputy.

GATE CADENCE (summary table - update per release):
- Gate: Alpha Readiness (T-60)
  - Purpose: validate integration points, test harness green
  - Owner: Lina Morales (eng-qa)
  - Acceptance KPIs: test-suite pass rate >= 95%, onboarding script executed in staging, basic latency p50 < 1200ms for 2k tokens
  - Quick notes: early smoke found intermittent 429s on batch queue (INFRA-934)

- Gate: Canary Rollout (T-7)
  - Purpose: run live traffic at 1% (low risk) and validate behavior under load
  - Owner: Evan Park (sre)
  - Acceptance KPIs: error-rate (5xx + app-level rejects) < 0.5% sustained over 1h, token-cost variance ±10% vs baseline, CPU/GPU utilization within expected band
  - Canary probes: routing fallback test, KV-cache hit-rate >= 40% for repeated prompts, end-to-end trace tags present

- Gate: Ramp to 25% (T+0)
  - Purpose: scale throughput and validate autoscaling policies and burst capacity
  - Owner: Ben Hart (platform)
  - Acceptance KPIs: 99.9% availability, 95th latency <= SLO for route, error budget remaining >= 80% for the window, fallback route test passes

- Gate: Full Launch (T+1 to T+7)
  - Purpose: observe stabilization and monitor regressions in quality/cost
  - Owner: Aisha Kumar (product-ops)
  - Acceptance KPIs: quality sentinel (prompt set A/B) shows no regression > 2% in task accuracy, unit token cost within target, support queue < threshold (see below)

KPI TRACKER - canonical signals to check before each gate (use the dashboard links):
- Availability SLOs: p99 calls success rate, target 99.9% (owner: Evan Park)
- Latency SLOs: p95 and p99 for the primary route, p95 target depends on route (hosted API: p95 <= 350ms for 256-token avg)
- Error budget: percent used in last 30d (SRE dashboard)
- Quality sentinel: regression delta on seeded prompt set (owner: product-evals)
- Cost-per-token delta: measured vs planned budget (owner: finance-platform)
- CS signal: top-3 customer tickets and severity (owner: Sophie Li)
- Observability health: traces emitted with route/model tags, KV cache telemetry, cold-start rate

Decision checklist (for each gate) - minimal fields to capture decision:
- Gate name
- Time window and stakeholders in the bridge
- Metrics snapshot (link to dashboard)
- Go criteria satisfied? (yes/no) - list the KPIs that passed/failed
- Mitigations in-place? (yes/no) - quick bullet list with owners
- Decision recorded and comms: who announced, which channels (Slack/Status page)

Example: Canary decision (template filled)
- Gate: Canary Rollout, 2026-03-04 09:00-10:30 PT
- Bridge: #prodops-launch / on-call SRE (Evan) / product-ops (Aisha) / CS (Sophie)
- Snapshot: error-rate 0.22% (pass), p95 latency +8% vs baseline (pass), token cost +12% (warning)
- Mitigations: reduced canary weight by 0.5% to stabilize cost (owner: Ben), enable caching TTL bump (owner: Lina)
- Decision: proceed to Ramp 5% with monitoring escalation rule tightened (owner: Aisha)

Contingency runbook (fast actions to consider) - short list, pick 1 or 2 depending on failure mode:
- High error-rate / latency spike:
  - Immediate: shift canary traffic to fallback model variant (fast toggle) and reduce canary weight to 0
  - Short term: pause new sessions for affected route, enable strict rate-limiting for anonymous traffic
  - Owner: Evan Park / Ben Hart

- Unacceptable quality regression (seed prompts showing > 3% drop):
  - Immediate: promote prior pinned model version (rollback) and freeze model rollout paths
  - Notify: CS and impacted customers; open postmortem label
  - Owner: Product-evals / Aisha Kumar

- Cost overrun during ramp (> +20% unit cost sustained):
  - Immediate: cap maximum tokens per request at routing edge, enforce token quotas, reduce canary weight
  - Short term: enable quantized variant for non-sensitive tenants (if available)
  - Owner: Finance-platform / Ben Hart

Telemetry & dashboards to snapshot before gate:
- SRE availability dashboard (link) - p50/p95/p99, error breakdown by code
- Cost dashboard - token units, GPU hours, reserved capacity utilization
- Eval sentinel - seeded prompts + crowd eval samples
- Support dashboard - ticket volume and category

Open questions / unresolved items (T-13 notes):
- Who signs off on incremental committed capacity for Dedicated customers during canary bursts? (need finance escalation path)
- Do we have a documented rollback SLA for private deployments (air-gapped) where model promotion may take >24h?
- Investigate reduced KV-cache TTL side-effects on hallucination rate for long-dialog workloads (Lina to run experiment)

Next steps / immediate action items:
- Lina: attach latest canary test run logs to this doc (due T-6)
- Ben: confirm autoscaler scheduled scale policy across regions and add runbook snippet (due T-5)
- Evan: create a condensed 'bridge checklist' and circulate to on-call (due T-4)
- Sophie: draft customer comms template for partial rollbacks (due T-3)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc minimal; heavy-weight runbooks live in /playbooks/launch-runbooks but we need this for quick decisions during the week of release.
- If any gate flips to 'hold', capture the single root cause and clear next milestone. Avoid long checklists in the heat of the moment.

Revision history (brief):
- 2025-11-03: initial sketch (Aisha)
- 2026-01-12: added canary probe list + cost mitigations (Ben)
- 2026-03-05: updated gate KPIs and added contingency runbook (Evan)
